prerequisites: Find the head of the main subject, separating it from objects and modifiers.
Distinguish singular from plural; recognize the simple present and the base form of a verb.
explanation: Agreement links the main subject to its finite verb. Intervening of-phrases and relative clauses do not change the main head. In the simple present, a third-person singular subject normally uses a verb ending in -s; a plural subject uses the base form. Be uses is/are. A passive keeps agreement in is/are before the past participle. A negative uses does not/do not before a base verb.

worked.action: The handle [of the cupboards] is broken: handle is singular.
worked.justification: Cupboards belongs to a modifier. Select is, not are.

worked.action: The parcels [on the desk] arrive daily: parcels is plural.
worked.justification: Desk describes location, so it cannot select arrives.

worked.action: The teacher [who works with the pupils] checks the books.
worked.justification: Teacher heads the main clause; who heads the relative clause. Keep the two agreement relationships separate.

worked.action: The driver, along with the helpers, checks the tyres.
worked.justification: Along with is not the coordinator and; driver remains the singular main head.

worked.action: The driver and the mechanic check the tyres, when these are two people.
worked.justification: Two separate people joined by and create a plural subject.

worked.action: Neither of the keys fits; Each of the keys fits.
worked.justification: In the formal convention for these questions, Neither and Each are singular heads. Do not select a plural form from keys.

worked.action: Beside the pump stand three buckets.
worked.justification: The subject follows the verb in inversion. Three buckets is plural.

worked.action: The record of repairs is checked weekly; the records do not require copying.
worked.justification: The singular passive uses is checked. The plural negative uses do not plus base-form require.
